dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Run the replacement id through `_resolve(...)` before adding it to the scope set so it is canonical for the referencing-commit membership test, matching how descendants are handled.
evidence: close_scope.py:144 `resolved = _resolve(desc_id, tracker, ticket_view=ticket_view)` — descendants ARE resolved
src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py:282 `if resolved_cache[ref] in accepted:` — commit refs resolved to canonical before membership test

src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py:256 reducer resolves target_id best-effort only: `canonical = resolve_ticket_id(raw_target, tracker_dir)` inside a try/except that swallows failures, so a non-canonical target_id can survive into deps
dropped.finding: In expand_with_disposition_replacements the replacement id returned by replacement_target_for_closed_disposition is added to the scope set raw, without passing through _resolve() to canonicalize it, whereas its descendants ARE resolved. referencing_commits compares canonical-resolved commit refs against the accepted set, so a non-canonical replacement id (e.g. an alias target that the reducer failed to canonicalize) would silently fail to credit its own referencing commits while still crediting its descendants.
scenarios: A disposition link whose stored target_id could not be canonicalized by the reducer (tracker unset or resolver exception), where the replacement's landed commit references the replacement's canonical id
dropped.suggested_fix: Replace `expanded.add(replacement); queue.append(replacement)` with a resolve step: `resolved_replacement = _resolve(replacement, tracker, ticket_view=ticket_view) or replacement` and add/enqueue that, and use it as the descendant seed.
